paras: The police pursuit and clubbing of Cassius Coolidge took place in St. Louis, Missouri, on the evening of August 25, 1905, when policemen fired on Coolidge, a Black porter, during a four-block chase and clubbed him after his capture. Coolidge had just shot two Black men, Oscar and Harry Grimes, killing Oscar; the St. Louis Republic, the only paper found to report it, treated the episode as a shooting story.
According to the Republic, the shooting grew out of a fight among Coolidge, also a porter, and the two Grimes brothers the previous Thursday.

Shortly after 9 o'clock, Coolidge met the brothers at the mouth of an alley on the north side of O'Fallon street between Tenth and Eleventh streets and, the paper said, opened fire "without a word." Oscar Grimes died at the City Hospital and Harry Grimes was shot in the left groin and reported in critical condition.

Patrolman Patrick Somers arrived as Coolidge ran through the alley toward Cass avenue, called on him to halt, fired a shot in the air, and then fired at him. Patrolmen Dwyer, Ballard and Bene and Sergeant Meyers joined the chase over Cass avenue, Tenth street and O'Fallon street, while four officers fired revolvers and residents ran for shelter. Somers overtook Coolidge and forced him to surrender at revolver point; by the police account Coolidge then attacked Sergeant Meyers and was "clubbed into submission." None of the police shots is reported to have struck him, and the article does not describe his injuries from the clubbing.
No report of an inquest into Oscar Grimes's death, a charge against Coolidge, or any review of the officers' conduct appears in the coverage.

The St. Louis Republic ran the story on page 5 on August 26 under the headline "KILLS ONE NEGRO; DISABLES ANOTHER," with subheads stating that Coolidge "Shoots Two Men of His Own Race and Is Sub- dued by Police." Its account rested on the officers' version alone and called Coolidge "the big negro" and "the fugitive". No other white paper and no Black paper was found to have reported the episode.

reader.title: Police pursuit and clubbing of Cassius Coolidge
bases: Policemen fired revolvers at Coolidge as he fled and clubbed him 'into submission' after his surrender (A1); the killing in the episode was Coolidge's shooting of two Black men, not police action.
Only one report, in the St. Louis Republic, was found in either press (A1).

accounts.label: Police account as reported by the St. Louis Republic
accounts.gist: Coolidge shot the Grimes brothers, ignored an order to halt and a warning shot, was chased under fire, surrendered at revolver point, then attacked Sergeant Meyers and was clubbed into submission.

framing.detail: The Republic headlined the shooting ('KILLS ONE NEGRO; DISABLES ANOTHER') and described the police fusillade and clubbing as routine capture, giving only the officers' version.

sources.paper: The St. Louis Republic (St. Louis, Mo.)
sources.note: Only report: Coolidge shot Oscar and Harry Grimes on O'Fallon street, St. Louis; police fired on him in a four-block chase, overtook him, and clubbed him after he attacked Sergeant Meyers.
quotes: The fusillade from the revolvers of four policemen, as they ran for four blocks in pursuit of Cassius Coolidge, a negro, who had shot Oscar and Harry Grimes, two other negroes
When overtaken and forced to yield his weapon, Coolidge regretted his action and attacked Sergeant Meyers. He was clubbed into submission.
He yelled at the negro, but the fugitive refused to halt. One shot was fired in the air
The shooting was the outcome of a fight the three negroes had Thursday.
